summary: Defines an extension to the Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol that enables reporting and control of multi-hop forwarding by DLEP-capable modems. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Radios can tell routers about links. This lets them also report on and control paths with several hops.

questions: what is the dlep hop count data item
what does dlep hop control do
subtitle: A DLEP extension that lets a modem report how many hops away a destination is, and lets a router steer that forwarding.

tldr.problem: Some modems forward traffic through intermediate modems, but DLEP destination messages say nothing about the number of hops involved.
tldr.mechanism: The extension adds a Hop Count data item that modems send, and a Hop Control data item that routers send to request a direct connection, end one, reset, or suppress multi-hop forwarding.
tldr.outcome: Routers learn when multi-hop forwarding is in use and can ask the modem to change it, though what a router does with that information is out of scope.

facts.label: Hop Count field
facts.value: 8 bits; 255 means unknown, greater than one

today: RFC 8629 is a Proposed Standard from July 2019. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and it extends the protocol defined in RFC 8175.

sections.title: Why a Multi-Hop Extension
sections.content:
The Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol (DLEP, RFC 8175) carries link information between a modem and a router, and allows extensions. RFC 8629 defines one extension for modems that support mobile ad hoc network (MANET) forwarding, where destinations are reached through intermediate modems.

DLEP Destination messages can report reachable destinations, but nothing about the number or capacity of the hops. This extension lets a modem tell the router when multi-hop forwarding is in use, and lets the router ask the modem to change that behavior. Each modem that transmits data on the way to a destination counts as one hop.

The RFC warns that Hop Control can change connectivity and even make destinations unreachable. The mechanism reports such changes, but what a router does about them is out of scope.
sections.eli5: Sometimes a message hops through several radios to arrive. This extension lets the router find out how many hops, and ask for changes.

sections.title: Turning the Extension On
sections.content:
Use of the Multi-Hop Forwarding extension SHOULD be configurable. To say it is in use, an implementation includes the extension type value in the Extensions Supported data item, which is sent and processed as in RFC 8175. The Multi-Hop Forwarding extension type value is 1.

The extension defines three data items: Hop Count (modem to router), Hop Control (router to modem), and a Suppress Forwarding action carried within Hop Control.
sections.eli5: Both sides say they understand this extra feature, just like agreeing on a secret handshake before using it.

sections.title: The Hop Count Data Item
sections.content:
A modem uses the Hop Count data item (type 21, length 2) to give the number of modem transmissions needed to reach a destination. The minimum is 1, meaning the destination is directly reachable through the router's local modem. It SHOULD be carried in Destination Up, Destination Update, Destination Announce Response and Link Characteristics Response messages when the hop count is greater than one. If the item is absent, the router MUST treat the hop count as 1.

The 8-bit Hop Count field holds the number of hops. The value 255 means an unknown number greater than one. Zero means a Hop Control action has left the destination unreachable, and zero MUST NOT be used in any message other than a Link Characteristics Response. A reachable destination MUST have a value of at least 1.

The P bit says a destination is potentially directly reachable, for example by reaiming an antenna. When set, the router MAY request a direct link. The bit MUST be ignored when the hop count is 1. Reserved bits MUST be zero when sent.
sections.eli5: It is a counter: how many radios have to pass the message along. One means it goes straight there.

sections.title: Hop Control Actions
sections.content:
A router uses the Hop Control data item (type 22, length 2) to change connectivity to one destination or to apply multi-hop processing device-wide. It MAY be carried in a Session Update message (whole device) or a Link Characteristics Request message (one destination). The 16-bit action field has four values.

  • Reset clears earlier control actions, device-wide or for the destination, and restores configured behavior.
  • Terminate says a direct connection is no longer needed. It is per-destination only and MUST NOT be sent in a Session Update.
  • Direct Connection asks the modem to try for a direct link. It is per-destination only, and SHOULD be sent only where the hop count is above 1 and the P bit was set.
  • Suppress Forwarding stops multi-hop forwarding. Device-wide, traffic from the router goes only to destinations one hop away and other modems' traffic not meant for the router is dropped. For one destination, the router's traffic to it is sent only when it is one hop away, while forwarding of traffic from other modems continues as normal.

After a change succeeds, fails or is rejected, the modem MUST respond with a Link Characteristics Response (or Session Update Response) with an updated Hop Count. The modem MUST report newly unreachable destinations with Destination Down and changed ones with Destination Update. Failures can happen, for example when link characteristics cannot support a one-hop connection, and requests can be rejected by local policy.
sections.eli5: The router can say: try to go straight there, stop trying, go back to normal, or do not pass other people's messages along.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The extension adds no vulnerabilities beyond those in RFC 8175, but Hop Control deserves care. It can change which destinations are reachable, and the risk is more likely than with the Link Characteristics Request. Implementations may add configuration controls so Hop Control is used only as the operator intends. Implementations MUST support configuring TLS use as in RFC 8175, to protect setups where injection attacks are possible. A compromised or impersonating modem could suppress transmission by the router or by a switch that connects them.

IANA registered extension type 1 (Multi-Hop Forwarding) and data item types 21 (Hop Count) and 22 (Hop Control). It also created the Hop Control Actions registry: values 0 to 3 are the four actions, 4-65519 is Specification Required, 65520-65534 is Private Use and 65535 is Reserved.
sections.eli5: Because the router can change how messages travel, only trusted devices should be allowed to give those orders, and the link should be protected.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Zero when sent, ignored on receipt.

fields.name: Hop Count
fields.desc: Modem hops to the destination; 255 means unknown, greater than one.

items.label: Terminate
items.desc: Direct connection no longer needed (per destination only).

items.label: Direct Connection
items.desc: Try to set up a direct link (per destination only).

items.label: Suppress Forwarding
items.desc: Stop multi-hop forwarding, device-wide or per destination.
